key_insight: RadSight argues that reliable radiology MLLMs must first solve low-level visual perception—like location, size, and density—before higher-level diagnosis and reporting can be trusted.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could improve how AI supports radiology by making outputs more grounded in actual image evidence and less prone to perceptual errors.
method: Built Perception-Bench, a 1.13M-sample benchmark covering 2D and 3D radiology across six tasks.
Designed RadSight with dual 2D/3D encoders to preserve native spatial structure.
Trained the model with a four-stage curriculum: alignment, perception, diagnosis, and interpretation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that RadSight outperforms prior MLLMs across all six Perception-Bench dimensions and shows gains on public 2D and 3D medical benchmarks.
watch_item: Benchmark gains do not automatically guarantee real-world clinical robustness, especially across unseen scanners, institutions, and patient populations.
paper_title: RadSight: Towards Perceptually Reliable Multimodal Radiology Image Understanding
